payload.friendly_name: mission-shell: shared Svelte 5 shell over the MissionStatusClient port
payload.purpose_context: The mission screens and the MissionStatusClient port exist, but no host renders the screens with real navigation and live data. This mission builds the shared Svelte shell both hosts mount: routing and layout around the screens, state, the mapping from screen intents to reads and host actions, the refresh policy driven by the change stream, connection banners, and how the dashboard treats desktop-only intents. It touches no I/O and changes neither the port nor the screens. Tracked as mission-ui issue 18 under epic 16.
payload.purpose_tldr: Give Kitty Desktop and Kitty Dashboard one shared shell that routes between the mission screens, keeps their data current from the change stream, and shows clearly when the service is connecting, reconnecting or unavailable.

options: A (recommended): no picker on the dashboard; it opens straight into its one project, the picker and folder dialog are never mounted, and a stray desktop-only intent is ignored without error
B: the dashboard shows the picker with its one project; Open project shows a notice explaining how to open another project (Kitty Desktop, or restart the dashboard on another project root)
C: as B, and the notice also offers the restart command to copy through the host copy capability
payload.question: Kitty Dashboard serves exactly one project and cannot browse folders. What does the shell do there with the Projects picker and the desktop-only intents sk-request-open-project, sk-browse-folder and sk-confirm-open-project?

options: A (recommended): navigation (entering or re-entering the view) plus the window becoming visible or focused again as signalled by the host, plus a shell-owned Refresh button in the top bar host-actions area on Artifact and Ops destinations
B: navigation plus host-signalled visibility or focus only; no new button
C: navigation plus the Refresh button only; no focus trigger
payload.question: Artifact and Ops views are not covered by the change stream and refresh explicitly (Drift already has its own Rescan). What triggers that refresh?

options: A (recommended): Storybook stories for every connection-banner state and each layout composition, with approved baselines in the existing visual gate, flagged for design review because the banners are not in the prototype
B: interaction tests only (browser-mode tests against the fixture adapter); visual baselines deferred to the host missions
payload.question: How is the shell's own new UI verified: the connection banners, the refresh control and the composed layouts?

payload.question: Squad R1-02: what does an unavailable result do to a slot that already has data?

payload.final_answer: Keep the data and the view state (research R-06); clarify spec FR-005 in a dated amendment.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-10-15, relayed by the coordinator

payload.question: Squad R2-10: after a refused subscription, how are views refreshed on reconnect?

payload.final_answer: While live updates are off, each non-first connected is a shell-side resync: re-read the displayed set; open no new subscription.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-10-15, relayed by the coordinator

payload.question: Squad R4-01: which package entry exports MissionShell, mountShell and ShellHost?

payload.final_answer: The . entry stays port-only; a new additive ./shell export carries MissionShell, mountShell, ShellHost and the shell types; ./testing is unchanged.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-10-15, relayed by the coordinator

payload.question: Squad R6-05: does the Chromium shell test project get its own unit-tests plant?

payload.final_answer: Yes: one unit-tests plant in test/shell/** with a single failure-only token from an assertion message; counted, with the unit-tests leg time and timeout re-derived.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-10-15, relayed by the coordinator

payload.question: Squad R6-03: when are proof-leg timeouts derived?

payload.final_answer: IC-09 sets provisional timeouts from local measurements; a post-PR (landing) fold re-derives them from the PR's first CI run (#17 precedent).
